features.name: Renaming, finishing, archiving and deleting
features.what: The session menu renames and deletes a session; a row's buttons mark it done or archive it.
features.reach: The ... beside the session title above the chat, or the buttons a sidebar row shows on hover.
features.proof: The new title shows in the row and stays after a reload; a done session leaves In work; archive and delete ask to confirm, then the session leaves the sidebar and stays gone after a reload.

scenarios.title: Rename from the session menu updates the row and survives a reload
Mark done moves a session out of In work

features.proof: A click on the row's box outside the title opens it; Enter on a focused row opens it; Shift+click shows the session's chat in the right panel and keeps the current one open.

features.name: Renaming a session in its row
features.what: Double-click on a row, or Rename in its right-click menu, turns the title into a field; Enter, the check or a click elsewhere saves, Escape keeps the old title.
features.reach: Double-click a session row, or right-click it and pick Rename.
features.proof: The field holds the whole title selected, so typing replaces it; the saved title shows in the row and survives a reload; after Escape the old title is back.

features.name: A row's right-click menu
features.what: Right-click on a row, or Shift+F10 on a focused one, opens the session menu; from it the user pins the session, files it in a new folder, moves it to another project or exports it.
features.reach: Right-click a session row in the sidebar.
features.proof: The menu opens on the row; a pinned row carries the pin mark; New folder files the session in a folder named in place; Another project opens the Move session dialog; Export Markdown says the session was exported.

scenarios.title: Shift+F10 on the focused row opens its menu
Pin to Pinned puts the pin mark on the row; Unpin removes it
New folder from the menu files the session in a folder named in place
Move to > Another project opens the Move session dialog
Export Markdown exports the session

features.name: Pinning to a list on the phone
features.what: With a pin list of their own, Pin session in a phone row's menu opens the Pin to sheet: Pinned, each list, New list. The pick pins the session into that list.
features.reach: The phone's session drawer: long-press a row, then Pin session.
features.proof: Pin to opens with the list in it; after the pick the row stands under that list's caption and carries the pin mark.

scenarios.title: Pin session on the phone opens Pin to, and the chosen list holds the session

features.name: A row's hover buttons
features.what: Pointing at a row shows its buttons: Track as in work for a session that is not in work, and Archive, which turns into Delete while Shift is held and then deletes without asking.
features.reach: Point at a session row in the sidebar.
features.proof: Track puts the session under In work; with Shift held the button reads Delete, and its click removes the session with no dialog, for good.

scenarios.title: Track as in work puts a session under In work
With Shift held Archive becomes Delete and deletes at once, not to the Archive

features.name: What a row says about its session
features.what: A row shows a running mark and the elapsed time while the agent works, an unread mark, the turn's time and a bold title once a turn ends unseen, a shield or a question mark while the agent waits on the user, the goal mark while it works toward a goal, and a tooltip with the title and project.
features.reach: Watch a session's row while it works in the background; point at a row.
features.proof: Each mark shows in its state and leaves when the state ends: opening the session clears unread; Alt+click marks a read session unread and back.

scenarios.title: A background turn shows running, then unread until the session is opened

features.name: Requests from sessions out of sight
features.what: When an agent in a session the user is not looking at asks for a permission, asks a question or shows a page that waits for an answer, a toast says so and Open session takes the user there; in the session on screen the request shows in place, with no toast.
features.reach: Keep one session open while an agent in another one reads a guarded file, asks a question or shows a page that waits.
features.proof: The toast reads Permission needed, or the question's or page's title with Agent is waiting for your input; Open session opens that session with the request ready to answer; a request in the open session raises no toast.

scenarios.title: A permission asked in another session raises a toast whose Open session opens it, ready to allow
